title: Direct Imaging of Vacuum Fluctuations in a Two-Dimensional Bose-Einstein Condensate
author: Yansheng Zhang et al., University of Cambridge
key_claims: Vacuum fluctuations in a lab-made quantum field (2D K-39 BEC) directly imaged for the first time
Amplification protocol distinguishes vacuum fluctuations from thermal noise via frequency-dependent power-law decay
BEC tuned to simulate sine-Gordon relativistic quantum field, enabling laboratory study of theoretically intractable regimes
Platform suitable for probing false-vacuum decay, particle production, and topological defect formation
methodology: Two-dimensional potassium-39 Bose-Einstein condensate; internal-state coupling via radio waves; spin-field encoding; sudden quench amplification; direct imaging of local spin variations
key_risk: Preprint — not yet peer-reviewed. Thermal noise subtraction and BEC imaging systematics require independent replication. Sine-Gordon mapping validity depends on interaction parameter tuning.
next_experiment: Peer review and independent replication; extend to false-vacuum decay bubble nucleation experiments; connect to C9 Cluster 2 quantum gravity analog models (cf. Barontini entropic-time mini-universe)
notes: Strong L1 candidate pending peer review. The BEC-as-quantum-field approach is a powerful analog-gravity platform. Connects to primordial fluctuation seeding (Cluster 2) and quantum thermodynamics of de Sitter space (Cluster 7).
